newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - APRIL 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - APRIL 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Anglo American Platinum Corp (Amplats) , the world's largest platinum producer, is to merge with its three listed subsidiaries and launch a 1.6 billion rand expansion programme to lift output by 300,000 ounces to 2.1 million ounces in 2002.

- Democratic Party leader Tony Leon took the lead in an opposition onslaught in parliament, calling on President Nelson Mandela to declare a state of emergency to combat crime which had created an effective state of anarchy.

- Pharmaceutical heavyweigh SA Druggists will appear in the High Court later this year over claims that it fialed to pay a former employee millions for his minority stake in subsidiary SA Druggists International (SADI).
- The private sector would, for the first time in South Africa, be invited to tender to build and run seven new prisons, Correctional Services Minister Sipo Mzimela said.

- Beer drinkers will be paying SA Breweries 10 million rand over and above the excise duty increases announced in the last budget, because the taxman has decided to withhold a refund the group thought it would receive for overpaying last year.
- The Cape high Court has granted Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom leave to intervene in wine cooperative KWV's planned conversion into a public company.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Amplats said it would open a new mine near Rustenburg. It also announced that it intended to rebundle all of its platinum interests into one company.

- Sanlam Properties, the largest property investor and manager in South Africa, will cease investing in any city centres countrywide, until the situation in central business districts has improved. Most city centres are plagued by crime, he said, and tenants were had been moving out.
- The KWV was dealt a blow in the Cape High Court when Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom was authorised to intervene in its plan to convert from a wine cooperative to a public company.
- Leisure-Net , the diversified lifestyles group, is planning to strip off its food franchising interests Foodgro in a bid to sharpen focus on its core health and fitness division, sources said.

- A South African design team comprising Stauch Vorster and Gapp Architects has been shortlisted to undertake the overall architectural and urban planning design of a proposed $300 million waterfront project in Singapore.

- The privatisation of Sun Air suffered a setback when it emerged that bid by a consortium including Virgin [VA.CN] and the Bhekilanga black economic empowerment group was in danger of being disqualified because of a possible conflict of interest, sources said.
SAKE-BEELD
- Amplats is to start development of a new platinum mine in Rustenburg this year, at a cost of about 900 million rand.
- The statutory Financial Service Board has drawn up legislation to improve investor protection.
- Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom says the government has no intention of taking over the assets of the KWV wine cooperative.
- Sanlam Properties said it would make no new investments in central business districts in South Africa's large cities.
THE STAR
- The government has launched a series of high-density crime prevention operations as part of its measures to fight crime, President Mandela said.
- At least 181 Moslem pilgrims died and 800 were injured when a blaze ripped through 70,000 tents near Mecca in Saudi Arabia.

- Zaire's government accused the former prime minister Leon Kengo wa Dondo of stealing millions of dollars intended for the military and said it would launch an internation search for him, the latest twist in the country's chaotic political situation.
